stages.title: Steamers on the Rhine
stages.text: On 1 May the steamer Concordia makes her first run from Mainz to Cologne. Goods and letters move faster on the river, and the towed barges begin to lose their trade.

stages.title: Gas comes to Frankfurt
stages.text: Knoblauch und Schiele's new gasworks begins supplying private houses in Frankfurt. Gasworks may now be backed as ventures.

stages.title: Prussia's semaphore line
stages.text: Prussia's optical telegraph now runs from Berlin to Koblenz. It carries only government messages; merchants' news still comes by courier.

stages.title: Railway companies seek capital
stages.text: After the Nuremberg line, railway committees form across the German states. Railways may now be backed as ventures.

stages.title: The Taunus railway opens
stages.text: On 26 September the first trains run from Frankfurt to Hoechst. Carters and canal boats on the route begin to lose their trade.

stages.title: Trunk lines planned
stages.text: With the first lines paying, promoters plan long trunk railways between the states. Trunk railways may now be backed as ventures.

early.text: The house's own line has shown what railways can earn, and promoters come early to plan a trunk line through Frankfurt.

stages.title: A London gas company in Frankfurt
stages.text: The Imperial Continental Gas Association completes its gasworks on the Obermainstrasse. Gas lamps spread through the city's streets.

stages.title: Through trains to Heidelberg
stages.text: The Main-Neckar line now runs from Frankfurt to Heidelberg. River freight on the Main and Neckar feels the loss.

stages.title: The telegraph reaches Frankfurt
stages.text: Siemens and Halske's electric line from Berlin to the National Assembly in Frankfurt is open. News from Berlin now arrives the same day.
